summary: To push a signed execution environment from a local system, podman pull the image, podman tag it as <server-address>/<name>:<tag>, then podman push with --sign-by <gpg key> (and --tls-verify=false in the example). An unsigned image can only be pushed with whatever signature is already embedded, or pushed without signing.
questions: How do I sign and push an execution environment to automation hub with podman?
How do I tag an execution environment before pushing it to automation hub?
Can I push an unsigned execution environment to private automation hub?

answer_card.title: Push a signed execution environment with Podman
answer_card.answer_md:
1. Pull the image: `podman pull <container-name>`
2. Tag it: `podman tag <container-name> <server-address>/<container-name>:<tag name>`
3. Sign and push: `podman push <server-address>/<container-name>:<tag name> --tls-verify=false --sign-by <gpg key reference>`

Without signing: `podman push <server-address>/<container-name>:<tag name> --tls-verify=false`
